title: Nepal's disasters show the urgent need for climate finance
gist: A WEF piece argues Nepal, with 0.05% of global emissions, has lost roughly a quarter of annual GDP to climate disasters in 11 years; after the August 2026 Langtang glacier collapse killed 1,455+, reconstruction of $4-5bn should be financed by grants not loans, with hazard-appropriate early warning.

insights.claim: Nepal produces 0.05% of global emissions yet in 11 years has absorbed disaster losses equal to roughly one-quarter of annual GDP.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Illustrates the equity gap that underpins climate finance demands from vulnerable states.

insights.claim: The 26 August 2026 glacier collapse near Langtang Lirung killed at least 1,455, left 5,285 missing, with initial damage over NPR 400 billion ($2.6bn) and full reconstruction expected at $4-5 billion.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Sizes the fiscal hole for a small economy.

insights.claim: The flood destroyed close to 8% of Nepal's hydropower capacity (a sector supplying over 90% of its electricity and a main export earner) and hit the Rasuwa trade corridor to China and Kailash tourism routes.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Compounding revenue losses and slow rebuild times for hydropower.

insights.claim: Nepal's recoveries are interrupted by repeated shocks (2015 earthquake, 2017 floods, COVID -2.37% GDP, 2023 Jajarkot quake, 2025 protests costing NPR 98bn, 2026 flood), and the ADB has cut post-flood growth to 4.1% while the government debates debt capacity.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Shock cadence and debt limits constrain growth and sovereign credit.

insights.claim: Nepal's early-warning systems were built for monsoon and river floods rather than glacier collapse because limited fiscal space forces choices on which hazards to cover.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Fiscal constraints drive hazard coverage gaps.

insights.claim: Preparedness rather than hazard magnitude determines disaster outcomes: the Swiss Blatten slope evacuation (~300 people, one death) after decades of monitoring contrasts with Chamoli 2021 where 204 died with no system.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Monitoring investment is highly cost-effective for glacier hazards.
insights.quote: hazard magnitude alone does not determine disaster outcomes, preparedness does
insights.locator: What this should mean for the rest of the world

insights.claim: The authors propose grants over debt-deepening loans, monitoring built for the real hazard, and rebuilding standards that plan for the next disaster; Nepal's foreign minister says loans are 'ballooning compared to our GDP'.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Pressure for grant-based loss-and-damage finance at COP31.
